evals.prompt: I have a new Python project at /tmp/test-project with some markdown docs in a docs/ folder. Initialize a documentation wiki for it with domain 'backend-services'.
evals.expected_output: Creates wiki directory scaffold (wiki/, raw/, graph/, audit/, log/, outputs/, .wiki-cache/) and a valid wiki.config.yaml with domain set to 'backend-services'
expectations: Runs init_wiki.py script to create directory scaffold
Directory scaffold includes wiki/, raw/, graph/, audit/, log/, outputs/
wiki/index.md, wiki/summaries.md, and wiki/overview.md are created

evals.prompt: Ingest the file /tmp/test-project/docs/architecture.md into my wiki at /tmp/test-wiki/. The file describes our authentication system using JWT tokens and session management.
evals.expected_output: Creates a wiki page about the authentication system with proper frontmatter, tags, and summary. Updates summaries.md and index.md.
expectations: Source file is copied to raw/ directory
A wiki page is created with type 'concept' or 'summary'
Page frontmatter includes title, type, tags, sources, created, updated, summary
summaries.md is updated with the new page's summary

evals.prompt: I've ingested several docs into my wiki at /tmp/test-wiki/. Now query: 'how does authentication work in our system?'
evals.expected_output: Synthesized answer citing specific wiki pages, with inline links to sources
expectations: Reads summaries.md first for progressive disclosure
Loads only the most relevant pages (not all pages)
Answer includes inline citations to wiki pages
